category: Cave diving — fatal accident / body recovery
working_title: He Went 270 m Down to Bring a Body Home
alt_title: The Promise That Killed Dave Shaw
subject: Boesmansgat (Bushman's Hole), Northern Cape, South Africa. 8 Jan 2005: Dave Shaw died at ~270 m trying to recover the body of Deon Dreyer (died Dec 1994). Support diver Don Shirley was injured on his own dive and survived. Dreyer's body surfaced days later tangled in Shaw's line.
why_potential: Combines the niche's two strongest triggers: body recovery (Dive Talk 9.15M) and an extreme number (270 m, ~15-min descent vs ~12-h ascent). Covered repeatedly in long-form (MrBallen, doc 'Dave Not Coming Back') and in Shorts, including non-English ones, so demand travels. Few 3D-animated Shorts exist. A depth cross-section is ideal for our pipeline.

working_title: 13 Trapped Behind Kilometres of Flooded Cave
alt_title: The Rescue That Shouldn't Have Worked
subject: Tham Luang Nang Non, Chiang Rai, Thailand. 23 June 2018: 12 boys of the Wild Boars football team and their coach were trapped by monsoon flooding. British divers Rick Stanton and John Volanthen found them alive on 2 July. All 13 were brought out through flooded passages 8–10 July. Former Thai Navy SEAL Saman Kunan died on 6 July.
why_potential: Highest raw demand signal in the set: Zack D. Films' 3D Short was reported at ~60M views (unverified). It's a rescue with hope, so it's advertiser-safe and has a broad audience. Risk: heavily covered, so we need a fresh angle (one specific moment: the 'how many of you?' discovery or the sedated dive out).

working_title: Under the Ice, the Only Way Out Was Deeper
alt_title: Five Divers Went In. Three Came Out.
subject: Plura / Steinugleflåget cave system, Plurdalen, Rana, Norway. 6 Feb 2014: five Finnish technical divers attempted a traverse entering through a hole cut in river ice. Two died at the deep section (reported ~100+ m); three survived, one after many hours of decompression.
why_potential: Ice entry, a deep traverse with no easy way back, and a survivor forced to pass a body make a vivid story. Multiple long-form and Short versions exist, plus a feature documentary (2016). Plura's dive centre has complained that YouTube is full of misleading Plura videos (divers24.com), so an accurate, careful version can stand out.

working_title: Stuck Upside Down With No Way to Back Out

subject: Nutty Putty Cave, Utah, USA. 24 Nov 2009: John Edward Jones (26) became stuck head-down in a narrow passage. Despite a large rescue effort he died about 27–28 hours later. The cave was sealed with concrete, his body still inside.
why_potential: Biggest proven entrapment demand (FatalBreakdown 13.09M; Zack D. Films also animated it). It is dry caving, but the audience overlaps fully. Included as 1 of 2 allowed adjacent stories. Risk: very saturated, so our angle must be the rescue mechanics (the pulley that failed) rather than a straight retelling.

working_title: The Greatest Cave Diver Ever Tried to Reach 1,000 ft
alt_title: Sheck Exley's Last Dive
subject: Zacatón, Tamaulipas, Mexico. 6 April 1994: Sheck Exley, a pioneer of cave diving and author of its safety rules, died during an attempt to dive to ~1,000 ft (~305 m). Partner Jim Bowden turned back at about 925 ft (reported) and survived. Exley's body came up days later attached to the descent line (reported).
why_potential: The irony that the man who wrote cave diving's safety rules died in a cave is a strong curiosity gap. It pairs with the Shaw story (Shaw called Exley a hero, reported). A vertical cenote and a depth race are trivial to animate.

working_title: His Camera Kept Recording at 91 Metres
alt_title: The Blue Hole's Arch
subject: Blue Hole, Dahab, Egypt. 28 April 2000: 22-year-old diving instructor Yuri Lipski died after descending to ~91 m while filming. His camera was recovered and the footage is widely circulated (we will NOT use or trace it). The Blue Hole's 'Arch' at ~55 m has lured many divers, with deaths commonly reported as 100+ (disputed).
why_potential: 'World's deadliest dive site' is the topic of Dive Talk's 9.15M outlier. Lipski reaction videos exist (293K). The arch is cavern/overhead rather than a true cave but sits squarely with the cave audience. Ethical treatment is mandatory: focus on the arch trap and narcosis, not on the death footage.

subject: Tham Luang, Thailand, 6 July 2018: former Thai Navy SEAL Saman Kunan (38, reported) died after losing consciousness while returning from placing air tanks along the flooded route for the rescue. He is honoured as a national hero.
why_potential: A focused spin-off of the highest-demand story (Tham Luang), from an underused angle. Strong emotional core with a short, Short-friendly arc. Spin-offs from the same environment cut production cost.

working_title: He Vanished at 20. Divers Found Him 10 Years Later.
alt_title: Deon Dreyer's Ten Years in Bushman's Hole
subject: Boesmansgat, South Africa. December 1994: 20-year-old Deon Dreyer, part of a support team for a deep dive, blacked out during ascent and sank (reported). His body was found ~10 years later (28 Oct 2004) by Dave Shaw at ~270 m.
why_potential: A prequel to CAVE-01 that sets up a two-part arc. The '10 years later' gap is a strong curiosity hook (an inkl/Mirror headline on the 'body left for 10 years' angle exists).

working_title: She Explored Caves No One Had Seen. Then the Silt Came.
alt_title: Agnes Milowka and Tank Cave
subject: Tank Cave, near Millicent, South Australia. 27 Feb 2011: explorer and underwater filmmaker Agnes Milowka (29) died after becoming separated from her buddy in a restrictive section and running out of gas (reported). She had worked on the film 'Sanctum' (2011).
why_potential: A distinctive explorer story with a Hollywood connection. It shows silt-out and restriction, which our particle pipeline renders well. Lower demand evidence and higher sensitivity (recent, family) mean a respectful tribute tone.

working_title: The Deepest Underwater Cave on Earth Has No Bottom (Yet)
alt_title: Hranice Abyss: 400 m and Counting
subject: Hranice Abyss (Hranická propast), Czech Republic. The deepest known flooded cave. In 2016 a remote-operated vehicle reached 404 m. Later geophysical surveys suggested it may continue to roughly 1 km (reported).
why_potential: 'Bottomless' and 'deepest' superlatives are proven title formulas ('The Horrifying Incidents in This Bottomless Cave'). Pure geology means no victims and low ethics risk. Strong comparison visuals (Eiffel Tower and skyscrapers next to the depth).

working_title: A Pond Near Rome That Swallows Robots
alt_title: Pozzo del Merro
subject: Pozzo del Merro, Lazio, Italy (north-east of Rome). A deep flooded sinkhole whose surface is covered in green plants. A 2002 ROV reached about 392 m without finding the bottom (reported). It was considered among the deepest of its kind before Hranice.
why_potential: A companion to Hranice ('deepest' series). Lower story strength (no human arc) but very cheap to produce and loopable. A filler/series entry.

working_title: The Clearest Underwater Cave Is Under a Frozen Russian Field
alt_title: Orda: Diving Inside a Crystal
subject: Orda Cave, Perm Krai, Russia. Reported as the longest known underwater gypsum cave (several km mapped), famous for very clear water and white walls. Usually dived in winter.
why_potential: Visual spectacle: white gypsum walls and cyan water make it our most beautiful environment. Low story stakes, so it suits a 'cave-of-the-week' series or B-roll-heavy Short. Demand evidence is weak.

working_title: They Built a Robot Map of a Cave by Hand
alt_title: Wakulla Springs: Mapping the Dark in 3D
subject: Wakulla Springs, Florida, USA. In the late 1980s–90s US Deep Caving Team expeditions led by Bill Stone pushed deep into the system with experimental rebreathers and later a 3D 'digital wall mapper' (reported). The Woodville Karst Plain Project (WKPP) later extended exploration.
why_potential: A niche tech story with low demand evidence. It has a visual hook (a laser-scanned cave appearing) that our pipeline can make. Kept as a low-ranked option for variety.
